RESIDENTIAL PURCHASE AND SALE AGREEMENT

1. PARTIES. This Residential Purchase and Sale Agreement (this "Agreement") is made on May 9, 2026 between Thomas and Georgia Aldebaran, husband and wife ("Seller"), and Nadia Okonkwo, an unmarried person ("Buyer").

2. PROPERTY. Seller agrees to sell and Buyer agrees to buy the real property commonly known as 214 Fernbank Lane, Asheville, Buncombe County, North Carolina 28804, together with all improvements and all fixtures now attached, and legally described as Lot 17, Block 4, Fernbank Estates, Plat Book 42, Page 118, Buncombe County Registry (the "Property"). Included in the sale are the range, dishwasher, built-in microwave, washer, dryer, all window treatments, and the detached storage shed. Excluded are the dining room chandelier and the greenhouse benches.

3. PURCHASE PRICE. The purchase price is $612,000, payable as follows: (a) earnest money of $10,000, paid to the Escrow Agent within three (3) business days after the Effective Date; (b) an additional deposit of $15,000 within three (3) business days after expiration of the Due Diligence Period; and (c) the balance in cash or immediately available funds at Closing.

4. ESCROW AGENT. The Escrow Agent is Fernbank Title & Trust, LLC, 88 Merrimon Avenue, Asheville, North Carolina 28801. The Escrow Agent shall hold the earnest money in a non-interest-bearing trust account and shall disburse it in accordance with this Agreement or a court order.

5. DUE DILIGENCE PERIOD. Buyer has until 5:00 p.m. Eastern time on June 8, 2026 (the "Due Diligence Period") to investigate the Property, including inspections, surveys, appraisal, insurance, and loan qualification. Buyer may terminate this Agreement for any reason or no reason by written notice delivered before the end of the Due Diligence Period, in which case the earnest money shall be refunded to Buyer and neither party shall have further obligation except as expressly stated in Section 13.

6. FINANCING. This Agreement is contingent on Buyer obtaining a conventional loan of not more than $489,600 at an interest rate not to exceed seven percent (7%) per year with a term of thirty (30) years. If Buyer, after diligent and good-faith effort, cannot obtain a written loan commitment on those terms by June 22, 2026, Buyer may terminate this Agreement by written notice delivered on or before that date, and the earnest money shall be refunded to Buyer.

7. INSPECTIONS AND REPAIRS. Buyer may have the Property inspected by licensed inspectors at Buyer's expense. Seller shall provide access on reasonable notice and shall keep utilities on through Closing. Buyer's rights under this Section are exercised through the termination right in Section 5; Seller has no obligation to make repairs.

8. TITLE AND SURVEY. Seller shall convey fee simple marketable title by general warranty deed, subject only to recorded easements and restrictions of record that do not materially interfere with residential use, and to ad valorem taxes for the current year. Buyer may obtain a survey and a title commitment at Buyer's expense. If Buyer notifies Seller in writing of a title defect before the end of the Due Diligence Period, Seller shall have fifteen (15) days to cure it; if Seller does not cure, Buyer may terminate and receive a refund of the earnest money or waive the defect and close.

9. SELLER DISCLOSURES. Seller has delivered to Buyer the North Carolina Residential Property and Owners' Association Disclosure Statement and the Mineral and Oil and Gas Rights Mandatory Disclosure Statement. Because the dwelling was built before 1978, Seller has also delivered the federally required Lead-Based Paint Disclosure and the pamphlet "Protect Your Family From Lead In Your Home," and Buyer acknowledges the ten (10) day opportunity to conduct a risk assessment, which Buyer waives.

10. CLOSING AND POSSESSION. Closing shall occur on or before July 10, 2026 at the offices of the Escrow Agent. Seller shall deliver possession of the Property, broom-clean and free of personal property and debris, at Closing. Real property taxes, homeowners' association dues, and rents, if any, shall be prorated as of the Closing date. Seller shall pay the excise tax and the cost of curing title defects; Buyer shall pay recording fees, loan costs, and its own attorney's fees.

11. CONDITION AT CLOSING; RISK OF LOSS. Seller shall deliver the Property at Closing in substantially the same condition as on the Effective Date, ordinary wear and tear excepted. If the Property is materially damaged before Closing, Buyer may terminate this Agreement and receive a refund of the earnest money, or close and receive an assignment of the insurance proceeds.

12. DEFAULT. If Buyer defaults, Seller's sole and exclusive remedy is to retain the earnest money as liquidated damages, the parties agreeing that actual damages would be difficult to determine and that this sum is a reasonable estimate and not a penalty. If Seller defaults, Buyer may terminate and receive a refund of the earnest money, or seek specific performance, and in either case may recover reasonable attorneys' fees.

13. SURVIVAL. Sections 9, 12, 13, 14 and 15 survive Closing or any termination of this Agreement.

14. GOVERNING LAW; VENUE. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of North Carolina. Any action arising out of this Agreement shall be brought in the state courts located in Buncombe County, North Carolina.

15. GENERAL. Time is of the essence. This Agreement is the entire agreement between the parties and may be amended only in a writing signed by both. Notices shall be in writing and delivered by hand, overnight courier, or electronic mail to the addresses below. This Agreement may be executed in counterparts and by electronic signature. This Agreement binds and benefits the parties and their heirs, successors, and permitted assigns; Buyer may not assign it without Seller's written consent.
